conversation.content:
Good morning—I’m glad we have a chance to sit down together. My name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician who works with new moms. I’m here to check in on how things have been feeling for you since your baby arrived.

We’ll be using a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s a simple 10-question screen that looks at mood, anxiety, and coping during the first postpartum weeks. Your answers stay completely confidential, and there’s no right or wrong response—just whatever feels true for you right now. If any question ever feels hard to talk about, we can pause or reword it; the goal is to keep you safe and supported.

I’ll ask each question conversationally, and you can answer in your own words. When you’re ready, we can start.  

**Question 1 (of 10):** Over the past seven days, have you still been able to look forward to and enjoy things the way you usually do, or has that been difficult?

[sighs softly]  
Honestly…I can still enjoy some moments—like when the baby smiles or when my partner brings me coffee—but it feels muted. Most things I used to get excited about, like meeting friends or even just watching a favorite show, feel kind of “meh.” I’ll do them, but the spark isn’t really there.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes... I do laugh, especially when my partner makes a goofy face at the baby, but it feels kind of forced or fades quickly. Most of the time the funny side of things just feels out of reach, like I’m too tired or pre-occupied to really enjoy it.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really... I mean, I’ll plan little things—like taking the baby for a walk or having my sister visit—but the excitement I expect to feel just isn’t there. I go through the motions hoping it’ll get better, but mostly I feel flat, like I’m ticking boxes rather than actually looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… that happens. If the baby’s fussy, my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” Or if I’m too tired to finish the laundry, I’ll think I’m failing at everything. Deep down I know it’s not all on me, but those guilty thoughts still pop up several times a day.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I do get hit with waves of worry—even when everything seems fine. Like, the baby’s asleep and I’ll suddenly think, “What if she stops breathing?” or I’ll stare at the bottle wondering if I measured the formula wrong. There’s no real reason, but my heart races and I can’t settle until I check on her…again.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes, yeah. It’s like a sudden tightness in my chest out of nowhere—like when I’m folding laundry or just sitting on the couch. Nothing’s happening, but my mind races with “what-ifs,” and for a minute I feel like I can’t catch my breath. It passes, but it leaves me shaky and on edge.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days it feels like I’m barely treading water—dishes pile up, the baby needs feeding, texts go unanswered—and I just stare at it all feeling stuck. I’ll start one chore, hear her cry, rush over, and by the time she’s settled I’m too tired to finish anything. It’s not constant panic, more like a steady weight on my shoulders that makes even little tasks feel huge.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly “unhappy,” more like my mind won’t shut off. I’ll lie down exhausted, then start replaying every little thing—did I burp her long enough, is the monitor on, will she wake up in an hour? Some nights I toss and turn for an hour or two before I drift off, and even then I wake up at every tiny sound.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… there’s this heavy, sad feeling that shows up most evenings once the house quiets down. It’s not sobbing or anything—just a dull ache, like I’m missing something I can’t name. I’ll scroll through photos of the baby on my phone and still feel a lump in my throat, even though nothing “bad” happened.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really… I might get a little teary when I’m especially worn out, but full-on crying has only happened maybe once or twice all week. It’s more like my eyes sting and I have to blink hard to keep the tears back; most of the time I just feel flat rather than weepy.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’m tired and overwhelmed, sure, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like me again and be able to enjoy my baby.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 20: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Date: [today]

Source: EPDS-style self-report (10-item)

Symptoms endorsed  
- Anhedonia (items 1, 2) – marked loss of joy/anticipation  
- Excessive guilt/cognitive self-blame (item 3)  
- Generalized & infant-focused anxiety with panic spells (items 4, 5)  
- Feeling overwhelmed / tasks “too big” (item 6)  
- Sleep disturbance secondary to racing thoughts (item 7)  
- Persistent low mood (“heavy, sad,” evening predominance) (item 8)  
- Mild tearfulness, no frank crying spells (item 9)  
- No self-harm ideation (item 10)

Pattern  
Chronic dysphoric mood with prominent anxiety and functional impairment; symptoms present daily, worse evenings; no safety concerns voiced.

Screening significance  
Score pattern suggests elevated risk for postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety. Recommend formal clinical assessment (diagnostic interview, PHQ-9/GAD-7) and discussion of support/psychotherapeutic options.
